title: API Fidelity Lab: lattice litmus for streaming + tool-calls + structured outputs
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an end-to-end API Fidelity Lab ("lattice litmus") that executes representative golden user scenarios across streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured-output code paths and gates PRs in CI. The lab will: (1) define a compact set of golden prompts and scenario templates that exercise interleaved streaming + tool calls and schema-validated structured outputs; (2) execute those scenarios against runtime variants (hosted/dedicated/private) and model shim layers to detect behavioral drift; (3) fingerprint canonical responses and flag semantic/serialization regressions (schema validation failures, truncated streams, tool-call id mismatches); (4) integrate with GitHub Actions to block merges for regressions above a tolerance threshold and surface detailed diffs to PRs and Console dashboards. Deliverables: golden scenario corpus, runner harness, CI workflow, failure classification UI snippets, and a follow-up plan for automatic rollback/fallback policies.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: scoped initial corpus to 12 scenarios (4 streaming-only, 4 streaming+tool, 4 structured-output + tool-call interleaving). Attendees: Maya, Avery, Jin, Priya.

2026-02-27 - Design review: decided to keep golden prompts in an internal git repo (redwood/golden-corpus) and store large fixture inputs in S3 to simplify CI checkout. Action: Avery to draft runner API by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-03 - Engineering spike completed: implemented a prototype runner that replays multiplexed stream fragments and records event traces. Found two issues with current stream reconnect semantics; filed ENG-62356 and ENG-62357 as follow-ups.
2026-03-05 - PM feedback (Diego Alvarez): include scenario-level customer impact metadata and map to Console alerting rules for high-severity regressions.

2026-03-08 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287 (litmus runner + basic CI). Requesting review from infra and runtime owners. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287

2026-03-10 - Risk decision: we will treat serialization/ndjson schema breaks as P0 CI failures; non-deterministic tokenization drift will be flagged but allowed with a higher tolerance and manual triage step.
2026-03-10 - Next: add structured-output JSON-schema checks and wire up per-scenario flakiness counters into our CI dashboard. Avery to pair with Jin on schema validator implementation.\n
